title: Transit routes and tickets
source: Original. Covers the ideas in the CS2103/T additional Part 1 practice (A and B): interface inheritance, a self-association, a bounded composition, a two-way association and a static method's parameter dependency.
author: soc-pe-script

code.text:
public abstract class Entry implements Searchable {
}

parts.prompt: Draw a class diagram to represent the code. Show all attributes, methods, associations, navigabilities, visibilities, known multiplicities, and association roles. Show associations as lines.

relations.typeHint: Searchable extends Listable. One interface extending another is inheritance: a solid line with a hollow triangle.

mistakes.msg: Right direction, wrong line. Searchable extends Listable; it does not implement it. Between two interfaces, use a solid line, not a dashed one.

relations.typeHint: Entry implements Searchable: a dashed line with a hollow triangle.

mistakes.msg: Right direction, wrong line. Entry implements Searchable (a class implementing an interface), so the line is dashed.

relations.acceptNote: A plain association is accepted. Route creates its own Stops and never shares them, so composition (a filled diamond at Route) is the stronger answer.
relations.typeHint: Route keeps its Stops in an array field and creates them itself.

mistakes.msg: A hollow diamond (aggregation) means the parts can be shared. Route creates its Stops and nothing else holds them, so use composition: a filled diamond.
Close. The array holds at most 5 Stops, but the constructor always adds two, so a Route has 2..5 Stops.
The array size is the most a Route can hold, not how many it has. The constructor adds 2 Stops and addStop() stops at 5, so 2..5.
The array has room for only 5 Stops, so the upper bound is 5. The constructor adds 2, so 2..5.

relations.typeHint: Ticket keeps its Route in a field, and Route keeps the Tickets it sold in a list.

mistakes.msg: route is set in the constructor and is final, so every Ticket has exactly 1 Route.
A new Route has sold no tickets yet, so its count starts at 0: * (or 0..*).
A Route keeps a List of the Tickets it sold, so the multiplicity next to Ticket is *.

relations.typeHint: A Ticket keeps another Ticket in its transfer field: a line from Ticket back to itself.

mistakes.msg: transfer starts as null and is only set by setTransfer(), so a Ticket has 0..1 transfer, not exactly 1.
transfer is a single Ticket field, not a collection, so the multiplicity is 0..1.

relations.typeHint: Stop has no Route field. canAdd() only takes a Route as a parameter, so at most a dependency (dashed arrow).

wrongClass.Entry: This object is a Route. Show it as r:Route, its real class.

forbidAttrs.stops: The Stops are shown by the links to the two Stop objects. Don't also list them as an attribute.
forbidAttrs.sold: The sold Ticket is shown by the link to the Ticket object. Don't also list it as an attribute.

forbidAttrs.route: The Route is shown by the link. Don't also list it as an attribute.

extraObjectHints.Entry: There is only one route object. Show it once, as r:Route, not also as :Entry.
extraObjectHints.Searchable: Searchable is an interface that Route implements. It is not a separate object.
extraObjectHints.Listable: Listable is an interface. It is not a separate object.
extraObjectHints.Ticket: Only one Ticket is created. transfer is still null, so there is no second Ticket.
